_about: Bannerfield settings: rendering and what it costs. sound: the whole audio side -- false (or ?sound=0) never even creates the audio context, so nothing is synthesised. Edit and reload (served from source) or rebuild dist (python3 build/build.py). URL options (?half=1, ?cells=2, ?people=10 ...) still override these per visit.

renderer._about: antialias: the canvas' multisampling; maxPixelRatio: cap on the display's pixel ratio (1 = one render pixel per CSS pixel, the cheapest); reflect: a true planar reflection in the water -- one extra draw of the world, quarter size, only when water is within reach. OFF: it is built but not yet right (the water takes one flat colour, the sky, as if every pixel sampled the same spot), and it is the most expensive thing in the frame when it runs. ?reflect=1 to work on it, with ?reflect=uv / raw / mirror to see which link is broken. targetFps: the frame BUDGET the ms/frame readout is judged against (90 = 11.1ms; it does not drive the loop -- requestAnimationFrame follows the display's refresh, so the fps number can never pass it). uncapped: drive the loop off a timer instead, drawing as fast as the machine allows, so the fps number shows what is really left (?fps=N, ?fps=max, live: __dbg.setFps(n)). grassFringe: the pass that lets grass stalks stand over what they grow in front of -- a cart's wheels, someone's boots, the skyline (?fringe=0|1; ?grass=flecks turns the whole lawn back to flat flecks). near / far: the camera's clipping distances in metres (keep near below player.collisionRadius, or a wall you stand against is cut open)

composite._about: the SDF figures (animals, people). halfResolution: near figures drawn into a half-size buffer (Shift+M toggles live); halfDistance: metres for 'near'; cells: at most N x N screen cells per figure (1 = off), cellBig: figures at least this tall on screen (2 = the whole height) take all of them, smaller ones half as many each way; cellMin: below this screen size one cell; poseLodNear/Far: beyond these metres figures are posed every 2nd / 4th frame; marched3dDistance: marched 3D fillets within this many metres (0 = off), marched3dScale: their buffer scale; earlyExit: parts sorted nearest-first so a pixel stops once deep inside the surface it has won (same picture; no gain measured in the software renderer -- try it on a GPU); solidCells: a screen cell lying wholly inside one solid part (in front of all else there) tests that part alone -- big shapes filling the screen get much cheaper, same picture; occlusion: the buildings and the ground draw their depth alone into a small buffer first (occlusionScale of the canvas) and a figure whose whole bounding sphere is behind it is never drawn -- a villager behind a house costs nothing (?occlude=0|1)

textures._about: bakedTiles: architecture patterns read from baked mipmapped tiles (false: evaluated per pixel); parallax: stone, brick, roof tiles and carving get depth -- the relief walked in parallaxSteps layers (each one more texture read per wall pixel), fading out by parallaxFar metres; the relief is lit by the world's shading and throws its own short shadows (parallaxShadowSteps more reads, 0: none)

mirrors._about: planes: wall planes reflecting at once (each is one extra draw of the scene); reach: metres within which they reflect

paintings._about: the size of the pictures taken at the start for the palace and cathedral frames

crowds._about: how many of each are in the world

player._about: the player's own body: seen when looking steeply down or in a mirror; the camera sits eyeBehind metres in front of its eyes (selfBody false: no body); look: hover (the pointer turns the view with no button held, the screen edges keep it turning, L takes the pointer), drag (hold a button) or lock (click to capture). freePitch: the mouse looks up and down as well as left and right -- off, the head stays level and you turn only left and right (?pitch=free overrides). collisionRadius: how close you get to walls, bodies and trunks (m)

people._about: nose: a nose on human heads (one SDF part per person; the face reads flat without it -- the minotaur's bull nose stays either way)
